title: RF resonance: a real theoretical study, an external energy source
summary: Balezin and colleagues (2018) numerically studied the Great Pyramid's response to external radio waves with wavelengths of 200–600 m, approximately 0.50–1.50 MHz. Their simplified dielectric model exhibited resonant scattering and local electromagnetic field concentration in chambers and the substrate region.
limit: The study assumed evenly distributed ordinary limestone and no unknown cavities. It is not a measurement of an operating ancient device, evidence of intentional RF engineering, or a demonstration of power generation. Giza V uses an illustrative single-degree-of-freedom response and artistic field geometry; it does not reproduce the paper's electromagnetic solver or predict Giza's field strength.

title: Nile waterscapes: documented transport, hypothetical electrical coupling
summary: Palaeoenvironmental research reconstructs a former Khufu branch of the Nile beside the Giza floodplain. Its water levels supported navigation and transport of construction materials during pyramid building. Merer's surviving logbook records work and journeys associated with Tura and Akhet-Khufu.
limit: A navigable river branch and seasonal floods do not establish a hydraulic power plant, a conducting channel beneath the King's Chamber, or electrically useful coupling to the pyramid. The prototype's flood level is a scenario control and visual metaphor; it is not a historical water-level reconstruction or a computed groundwater model.

title: Stone and foundation: limestone, granite, and an explicit load scenario
summary: The Great Pyramid is predominantly limestone, with granite used in important interior elements and fine limestone in its original outer casing. Published Giza geology describes sedimentary limestone bedrock. The proposed vast quartz-crystal foundation is not established by these sources.
limit: The v5 architecture and material boundaries are procedural approximations, not a surveyed reconstruction. The user's 100,000 stones × two metric tonnes is a 200,000,000 kg thought-experiment load, not the mass or complete block count of the actual Great Pyramid. Stress requires contact area and load paths; mass alone does not determine voltage or useful electrical energy.

title: Quartz: genuine piezoelectricity, unverified site-scale power system
summary: Quartz can develop electric polarization under mechanical stress. Experiments also detect effects in quartz-rich rocks, with important dependence on grain distribution and fabric. Dielectric polarization, which concerns a material's response to an electric field, and piezoelectric coupling, which links mechanical strain and polarization, are different properties.
limit: A large static stone load is not a continuing power supply. Loading can create charge; leakage and a connected load dissipate it. Sustained output requires changing stress and an energy source. Electrode geometry, capacitance, leakage, effective crystal orientation, and mechanical coupling are unspecified for the proposed pyramid system. The inherited RC trace is dimensionless and illustrative, with no prediction in volts, watts, or joules.

title: Conductive pathways: an invented experimental configuration
summary: Copper artifacts and fittings are reported in the Giza context, but they do not establish a continuous iron, copper, or gold lining of the Great Pyramid. A historic iron-plate find has a contested interpretation; British Museum researchers reported no detected gold and argued that its structure was compatible with post-medieval ironworking.
limit: The prototype's continuous conductors and their precise ratios are proposed additions. Their appearance does not certify ancient wiring, a missing gold surface, or an intentional conductive/insulating circuit. Real conductive layers may shield fields, introduce loss, or change resonant modes; a decorative brightness change is not a conductivity calculation.

title: Wardenclyffe: historical wireless ambition, speculative Giza analogy
summary: Tesla developed Wardenclyffe beginning in 1901 as a proposed station for worldwide wireless communication and power transmission. Its surviving history supplies a compelling comparison with modern ideas about resonance, grounding, transmission, and ambitious infrastructure.
limit: The consulted authoritative histories do not establish that Wardenclyffe was a replication of the Great Pyramid. This edition treats that connection as a creative analogy. Wireless transmission redistributes energy from a source; resonance by itself does not supply an energy source or prove a proposed transmission system's efficiency.

title: Ankh and Was-sceptre: historical symbols, authored journey
summary: The ankh is associated with life and the Was-sceptre with dominion or power. The accepted story uses these two objects, with ankh near the heart and Was near the head, to stage a king's 108-second passage through a luminous Duat. Witness and First-person cameras offer switchable views of the same authored event.
limit: Symbolic power does not establish electrical technology. The precise figure, pose, placement, materials, luminous device coupling, chamber ornament, and journey are artistic inventions. Later Egyptian objects inform visual language without proving their presence in Khufu's chamber. No reliable evidence is supplied for an electrical ritual, consciousness transfer, or supernatural journey triggered by RF fields; first-person body hiding is a camera technique.

title: The encounter: geometry, ancient craft, and nonhuman presence
summary: The accepted cinematic fiction escalates from cosmic geometry to ancient machinery and craft, then to a nonhuman encounter. A maximum encounter level of geometry, craft, or beings lets the viewer cap the reveal; beings is the default and permits all three stages. Choreography and reveal depend on journey time, including when seeking directly to a scene.
limit: The machines, craft, nonhuman figures, their apparent antiquity, and their divine or alien implications are authored fiction. No evidence of alien authorship or an alien machine is provided. Archaeological records, workers' settlements, construction marks, and transport documents support ancient Egyptian human agency. Choosing a fuller encounter changes the story's visibility, not its evidence tier.

title: Sky altitude: ionosphere and the fictional two-mile canopy
summary: NASA describes the ionosphere as a variable ionized atmospheric region extending from roughly 48 km upward. Two international miles is exactly 3.218688 km, within the troposphere rather than the ionosphere. Giza V names that low fictional setting a storm canopy and offers an 80 km ionospheric-sheet reference.
limit: The reference sheet is a chosen scenario height, not a universal boundary. The sky is drawn with explicit vertical compression. Its mesh, apparent arc length, and changing altitude do not calculate real electric breakdown, collection current, or an actual conducting connection to Giza.

title: The global atmospheric circuit: maintained potential, bounded current
summary: Atmospheric-circuit research describes thunderstorms and electrified shower clouds maintaining an ionospheric potential of about 250 kV relative to Earth. Fair-weather conduction current density is only a few picoamperes per square metre. These quantities describe a distributed global circuit, not a local utility supply.
limit: A large potential difference alone does not establish available power; current and continuing energy input also matter. A sustained-looking arc needs supplied energy. Giza V enters its mythic MW/GW source explicitly and does not derive it from the global voltage. Dielectric response describes how a material polarizes in an electric field; it is not a separately flowing fuel called dielectricity.

title: Capacitance, stored energy, and output power have different units
summary: An ideal capacitor stores energy E = one half C V squared, with capacitance C in farads, voltage V in volts, and energy E in joules. Power in watts is energy per second. Giza V uses an assumed rated lumped reservoir and tracks explicit initial precharge, input, delivered output, dissipation, and storage limits.
limit: The capacitance and voltage are operator assumptions, not measured properties of Giza or an Earth-ionosphere collector. A full 10 microfarad reservoir at 50 megavolts contains 12.5 gigajoules; that energy is not 12.5 gigawatts. The displayed regional grid is schematic, and no archaeological gigawatt supply is established. Initial precharge and each later supply must appear in the energy ledger.

title: Earth's Tesla Coil: a resonant-circuit analogy and a mythic machine
summary: Tesla coils illustrate resonant circuits and magnetic induction driven by an external energy source. Giza V borrows that conceptual vocabulary for an imagined planetary machine, with a separate lumped LC response and an inspectable reservoir. Tesla's historical wireless-transmission ambitions provide context rather than a Giza design record.
limit: The simple LC model is not a complete coupled Tesla transformer, a Maxwell/plasma calculation, or a proof of global wireless power transmission. Resonance does not create the reservoir's energy. The sky arcs, planetary coil, Upper Egypt beacon network, ancient machinery, craft, and nonhuman encounter are authored fiction; no evidence that Tesla replicated Giza is supplied.
